kitDescription: Sin is an Electric assault-rifle Defender and Burst II tank whose kit is almost entirely survivability and gauge economy. Every time she fires the last bullet of her magazine she briefly gains Max HP equal to 15.03% of the highest-Max-HP ally's HP for 5 seconds and taunts all enemies. Whenever any team Full Burst ends, her own burst gauge fills 16.17% faster for 5 seconds, arming the next rotation. Her burst skill damages enemies within attack range for 176.32% of her final ATK, and each time she casts it she climbs an escalating defensive ladder: lifesteal from the first cast, increased incoming healing from the second, and a DEF boost from the third onward. The burst also carries a Damage Taken debuff on all enemies, but only when more than four non-Nikke enemies are present — a condition that is never met against a single raid boss, so it never fires at scope.

Raw S5 file collected 0 tests (four payload-shape RECON_ERRORs: ov.blocks vs bare arrays, .slot vs .position, srcSlot as index vs slot-name, .buckets vs .breakdown) — recon errors, not faithfulness divergences; the mechanical-only adapted copy passes 20/20 with 4 self-declared GAP skips.

verdictRationale: [judge score string: 1.0 (8/8 kit lines FAITHFUL or DOCUMENTED_GAP)] No real gotchas. All five load-bearing lines are FAITHFUL with live-fire confirmation and working counterfactual discrimination: the last-bullet Max-HP duplication (cadence pinned against engine reload events, basis honestly declared undecidable via the roster-tie rather than fake-discriminated), the fullBurstEnd gauge window (frame-exact, fullBurstEnter mis-key fails), the cumulative burst-usage escalation (instant-max and cast-3-only both fail; the count-based gate keeps step 3 on cast 3 despite the unmodeled step 2), the FB-exempt 176.32% nuke (correctly NOT folded under the >4-enemy header, level-1 magnitude fails), and — highest-leverage — the >4-enemy Damage Taken debuff correctly never-on at single-boss scope with an absence canary and a proven ungated-inflation counterfactual. The three deliberate skips (taunt, incoming-healing step, gated debuff) are documented verbatim with precedents and recipes. The blind re-derivations converged: S6's skill1 and gauge blocks are byte-identical to the driver's, and every S5 divergence is a RECON_ERROR (four payload-shape crashes in the raw file plus one null-vs-undefined assertion — the mechanical adapted copy passes 20/20 with its 4 self-declared GAP skips), not a faithfulness signal. Two same-model residuals for the owner to spot-check: (1) the burst nuke's crit eligibility — S6 read crit:true off the generic formula table while the driver shipped non-crit per helm H7 / nero N6 flatDamage convention; precedent backs the driver but a one-line owner ruling would close it permanently; (2) the escalation blocks live in the burst slot rather than skill2 — behaviorally null (all payloads are non-damage, so the skill-slot/burst-slot FB-ordering distinction cannot bite) but worth a hygiene note. Nothing must change for GO.
